holidays.name: International Dance Day
holidays.description: A worldwide celebration of dance in every form, from ballet and breakdancing to the chicken dance at weddings. Studios, theaters, and street corners fill with people who just can't keep their feet still.
holidays.origin: Established in 1982 by the International Dance Council, a UNESCO partner, and the International Theatre Institute. April 29 was chosen to honor the birthday of Jean-Georges Noverre, the creator of modern ballet.
holidays.funFact: Each year a different choreographer or dancer from around the world is chosen to write an official International Dance Day message.

holidays.name: National Shrimp Scampi Day
holidays.description: A day for savoring shrimp swimming in garlic, butter, white wine, and lemon, ideally piled over linguine, with a side of bread for sopping up every last drop.
holidays.origin: A food-industry observance that grew out of the popularity of Italian-American restaurant cuisine. The dish evolved in the United States from Italian cooking traditions.
holidays.funFact: In Italian, 'scampi' actually refers to a type of small lobster, so 'shrimp scampi' is technically 'shrimp shrimp-ish lobster.'

holidays.name: Zipper Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble zipper, the clever clasp that keeps our pants up, our jackets closed, and our dignity intact. Celebrate by zipping and unzipping things with extra appreciation.
holidays.origin: Commemorates the patent anniversary of the zipper. Whitcomb Judson patented his 'clasp locker' in the 1890s, and Gideon Sundback later perfected the modern design in 1917.
holidays.funFact: The word 'zipper' was coined by B.F. Goodrich, who used the fasteners on rubber boots and liked the zip sound they made.

holidays.name: Superhero Day
holidays.description: A caped-and-masked celebration where fans dress as heroes, binge movies, and debate who would win in a fight. Everyday heroes get recognized too.
holidays.origin: A pop culture observance popularized by comic book fans and retailers, with a fan-driven tradition of marking it in late April.
holidays.funFact: Superman's debut in Action Comics #1 in 1938 launched the superhero genre, and a copy of that issue has sold for millions of dollars at auction.

holidays.name: Arbor Day Observance Week Kickoff: Hug a Tree Moment
holidays.description: Late April is prime tree-appreciation season, and this quirky unofficial observance encourages you to go outside and embrace your nearest tree, with or without witnesses.
holidays.origin: Rooted in the Arbor Day tradition begun in Nebraska in 1872 by J. Sterling Morton, which spread tree-planting celebrations across the United States each spring.
holidays.funFact: On the first Arbor Day, Nebraskans planted an estimated one million trees.
